prompt.context: Your client, Ikoyi Co, is a UK-based company selling skincare products. They have been successful in the UK and are considering entry into the US. They have asked us to help identify if this is a viable strategy and which key US markets to enter.
prompt.question: Is entering the US market a viable strategy for Ikoyi Co, and which key US markets should they enter?

clarifying_info.q: What is the revenue goal for the US?
clarifying_info.a: The client is looking for $500M Net Sales Value in 3 years, after retailers take their cut (40%). The imagined split is 50% DTC (no margin cut, 100% revenue retained) and 50% retail.

clarifying_info.q: What products does Ikoyi Co sell?
clarifying_info.a: General skincare products, e.g. moisturizers, vitamin C serum, exfoliators.

clarifying_info.q: How does Ikoyi Co earn revenue?
clarifying_info.a: Directly to final consumers on their website (DTC) and through retail channels.

clarifying_info.q: What is Ikoyi Co's position in the UK?
clarifying_info.a: Currently one of the biggest players in the UK market. The industry is very fragmented.

clarifying_info.q: Are we considering markets outside the US?
clarifying_info.a: No, the company is considering the US only.

exhibits.title: US Skincare Market by Region ($M)
exhibits.shows: A stacked bar chart showing the US skincare market broken down by four regions (East, West, Midwest, South) with each bar split by competitor market share (Yo Yo Skin, Glow Inc., Never Age Inc., Skin Pro, Others).

exhibits.title: Region Market Size and Potential Market Share (Year 1–3)
exhibits.shows: A table showing total market size in Year 1 for each region and Ikoyi Co's potential market share in Year 1, Year 2, and Year 3.

framework: Economics: Profit potential (revenue in US, cost of operating in US); Investment required (upfront costs, payback period); Market size, growth, and competitive environment; Consumer preferences and industry trends
Company Competencies: Brand power to attract customers; Staff skills and expertise; Supply chain capabilities; Channel access — retail shelf access and DTC/digital marketing capabilities
Other Considerations: Regulations (e.g. FDA compliance); Macro-economic risks; Taxation; Political risk; Currency risk

questions.prompt: Look at Exhibit 1. Which regions are most attractive for Ikoyi Co to enter, and why?
questions.guidance: Candidate should observe that the West ($750M) is the largest region but is highly concentrated — Yo Yo Skin holds ~68% share, plus Glow Inc. ~24%, leaving very little room for a new entrant. The other three regions (East, Midwest, South) are smaller but significantly more fragmented, making them more attractive for a new entrant. Candidate should eliminate the West as a priority entry market.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, calculate Ikoyi Co's expected gross revenue in Year 3 across the three most attractive regions (excluding West). Does this meet the $500M Net Sales Value target?
questions.guidance: Candidate should apply 10% annual market growth to each region, then multiply by the Year 3 market share to get Ikoyi's Year 3 revenues. Then work backwards: the $500M target is net sales value after the 50/50 DTC/retail split and 40% retailer cut. Gross revenue goal must first be derived. Candidate should also recognize that even if all four regions are included, the target may not be met.

math.setup: Step 1: Work backwards to find required gross revenue (X). Revenue = 50% DTC (full revenue) + 50% retail (60% of revenue after 40% retailer cut). So: 0.5X + 0.5(0.6X) = 500M → 0.5X + 0.3X = 500M → 0.8X = 500M → X = $625M gross revenue required. Step 2: Grow each regional market at 10%/year for 2 years to get Year 3 market size. Step 3: Multiply Year 3 market size by Year 3 market share for each region.
steps: $365M < $625M gross revenue required → Revenue target is NOT met even entering all 4 regions
math.answer: Entering all four regions yields approximately $365M in gross revenue in Year 3, well short of the $625M gross revenue needed to achieve the $500M net sales target. The revenue goal is unattainable through regional expansion alone — lead into brainstorm.

questions.prompt: [Brainstorm] The revenue target cannot be met through regional market entry alone. What other ways could Ikoyi Co reach their $500M net sales target?
questions.guidance: Candidate should generate MECE buckets — typically Price, Quantity/Volume, and New Products/Channels. Strong answers include both incremental and transformational ideas.

brainstorming.prompt: What are other ways the client could reach their revenue target?

categories.name: Price
ideas: Increase price of skincare products sold
Implement tiered pricing based on customer loyalty
Renegotiate percentage/price terms with retailers to retain more revenue

categories.name: Quantity / Volume
ideas: Increase quantity of products sold by gaining more final consumers and retailers
Explore B2B model — partner with hospitals, dermatologists, or spas
Explore company-owned physical retail stores as an additional channel
Expand into additional US regions or sub-markets beyond the initial three

categories.name: New Products / Services
ideas: Create new product lines (e.g. premium or clinical skincare)
Expand into adjacent beauty or wellness categories

categories.name: Marketing
ideas: Increase marketing efforts via social media and influencer partnerships
Educational outreach campaigns to build brand awareness and trial

recommendation: Option A (Enter): Yes, Ikoyi Co should enter the US market, beginning with the three most attractive regions (East, Midwest, South) and potentially the West. Ikoyi is a powerful brand in the UK which may translate to an American audience, and they can leverage existing product and operational capabilities.

Option B (Do Not Enter): No, the US market should not be entered at this time. Even entering all four regions falls short of the $500M net sales target, and a nationwide launch introduces significant logistical, supply chain, and upfront marketing costs. However, there is a risk of missing access to new customers and brand growth.
Candidate should commit to one recommendation with supporting rationale.
risks: Yes (Enter): Establishing new international supply chains; FDA regulatory compliance; competitor retaliation; currency and political risk; under-estimated upfront costs
No (Do Not Enter): Forfeiting potential new revenue streams and customer access; diminished brand presence if a US competitor enters the UK market; lost first-mover advantage
next_steps: Perform feasibility studies and stress-test key assumptions (market share projections, growth rates)
Conduct due diligence on new suppliers and logistics partners
Explore additional revenue levers (pricing, B2B, new channels) to close the gap to the $500M target
